title: Packers, tight end Tucker Kraft agree to contract extension: Sources
content:
The Green Bay Packers and tight end Tucker Kraft have agreed to a four-year, $75 million contract extension, with a maximum value of $92 million and a $26.5 million signing bonus, per league sources who were not permitted to speak on a deal that was not yet finalized.

Kraft, a 2023 third-round pick out of South Dakota State, will play in a game Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings for the first time since tearing his ACL last season in Week 9.

From Weeks 1-8, Kraft ranked third among tight ends in receiving yards, tied for second in touchdown catches and first in yards after catch per reception. He said in June that he thought he was the league’s best at the position when his season ended. Kraft has 113 catches for 1,551 yards and 15 touchdowns with 9.1 yards after catch per reception in three seasons.

Kraft said earlier this offseason that he wanted to be a Packer for life, and this brings him one step closer to that goal. Monday, teammates voted Kraft a captain for the second consecutive season.

Kraft becomes the third Packers pass catcher to ink a hefty contract extension this offseason after wide receivers Jayden Reed (three years, $50.25 million) and Christian Watson (four years, $92 million).
